answer: Sybil resistance here is ancestry capping, not slogans. A joining agent must fund its lockup from a disclosed payment river; the node records the prior twelve parent outputs. Those parents are wired into a collision trellis: any two live keys that share a parent inherit one combined seat, split by stake, so cloning cannot grow voting power. If an old relic address later buds fresh keys from the same outputs, the newest lockup is slashed 25% when the shared ancestor is finalized, making farmed identities strictly more expensive than a single honest seat.
